title: Prove the seven-ingress threshold for direct P104 chart-278 repair
body:
On the pinned #7786 rational word, **seven scalar ingresses from chart 3 are necessary and sufficient** to replace the 278 → 288 → 127 path by direct transmission from 278 to 127. Six fail even when all ten original ingresses and the other nine egress payloads at chart 278 are jointly recoded, and the 901 surviving receiver deposits are allowed to change as a result. The scoped lower bound also allows arbitrarily many additional scalar sends from the two original edge donors and from chart 278 directly to the receiver.

Just six exterior terminal operators force a rank-six constraint. One independently reconstructed nine-coordinate input then makes the entire allowed chart stock and receiver observations vanish while the required terminal is one. With a seventh core ingress, a chronological program restores all 1,289 outputs. Its signed paid surcharge is **94.9667971064257… across 48 rational calls** at the enrolled target, with local arithmetic free. The selected exponent is unchanged.

Clear1nsight supplied the #7786 word and #7795 cut evidence, building on Ali Romman's #7776 framework. #7807 and #7808 treated direct sends and cooperative relays with surviving stocks frozen. This result addresses the joint recoding of the chart-278 boundary.

All 8 registered CPython 3.12 checks passed in the checkout and in a read-only, Git-free export. The commit, source history, file modes and exported inventory passed the repository checks.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-receiver-ingress-repair
```
